title: The Carpenter's Shed
story:
The morning began with the sharp, sweet tang of freshly cut cedar. From his perch on a low adobe wall, James watched the old carpenter work with slow, practiced grace. He watched the thin amber ribbons curl away from the hand plane. He watched the carpenter's calloused thumb test the bevel of a mortise. He watched the fine dust hang suspended in the cool highland light, smelling not like the heavy ink of the Grand Library, but like the deep green boughs of the mountains he had crossed.

When Don Tadeo paused to wipe his brow with a frayed cotton rag, he noticed James sitting quietly with his brass canister tucked against his flank. The old man smiled with gentle, crinkled eyes, set down his tool, and gestured with an open hand toward the overgrown path behind the shop. He did not rush, nor did he make any sudden noise. He simply walked toward the neglected wooden outbuilding huddled against the stone courtyard wall, leaving the heavy plank door swung wide to the sun.

James followed, his bare feet padding softly over years of scattered wood shavings and dry jacaranda blossoms. The shed was old and weathered to a soft, silvery slate, but its cedar posts were sound and its low red clay tiles were tightly fitted. Sunlight slanted through a cracked wooden shutter, illuminating an ancient workbench, a pair of rusted hinges, and a forgotten earthen floor swept clean by highland drafts. It was neglected, but it was dry, shielded from the afternoon showers that gathered over the peaks.

Don Tadeo leaned against the doorframe, patted the solid timber lintel twice, and nodded to James before turning back to his bench. Left alone in the quiet interior, James set his canister upon the edge of the worn workbench, feeling the smooth cedar beneath his palms. Outside, the steady scritch-scratch of the carpenter's plane resumed, rhythmic and steady, a reassuring heartbeat in the quiet village.
location: The Old Shed behind Don Tadeo's Workshop, Aldea San Gabriel
